title: Farm, Sektur, Lolcow, 4chan & Moloch Question Expansion
purpose: Make the Farm/Swamp/Sektur/Moloch branch discoverable through natural-language search questions while routing answers to canonical world/shadow records.

entries.question: What is the Farm in the Potatoverse?
variants: What does Farm mean?
What is Tim Dooley's Farm concept?
entries.short_answer: The Farm is a system metaphor for turning people, reactions, reputation and attention into repeatable harvest. It is strongest when classification, observation, archives, commentary and audience reward reinforce one another.
entries.deep_answer: The project now distinguishes Farm from simple hostility. A Farm is an attention-production ecology: discovery → classification → enclosure/thread → observation → event or reaction → capture → interpretation → archive → redistribution → renewed observation. The moral question is whether the process increases autonomy and future capacity or turns people into permanently harvestable subjects.

entries.question: Why is it called a lolcow?
variants: What does lolcow mean?
Where does the word lolcow come from?
entries.short_answer: Lolcow combines LOL with the metaphor of a cow that can be repeatedly milked: a person treated as a reliable source of amusement, reaction or drama.
entries.deep_answer: The word is important because it contains the Farm economy in miniature. The person is not merely disliked; they are classified as a renewable yield source. That classification can shape what observers look for, how reactions are interpreted and what kinds of intervention earn status.

entries.question: What is Da Sektur?
variants: What does Sektur mean?
What is the Sektur around Ethan Ralph?
entries.short_answer: In the relevant internet-subculture history, Da Sektur refers to the Ethan Ralph / Killstream / Internet Bloodsports drama milieu and its network of personalities, orbiters, rivals and audiences.
entries.deep_answer: The archive should treat Sektur first as a historically specific livestream-drama ecosystem rather than an occult category. From there it can be used symbolically for a conflict-centered identity ecology in which loyalty, enemies, clout, clips, commentary and cross-platform drama become organizing forces.

entries.question: Is a Sektur the same as a cult?
variants: Is Da Sektur a cult?
What is the difference between a cult and an online drama community?
entries.short_answer: No. Cult is a contested sociological/religious label, while Sektur is a specific internet-subculture term. It is more precise to test for high-control, self-sealing, charismatic, identity-fusing or dissent-punishing dynamics than to assume cult status.
entries.deep_answer: An online community can display some high-control features without being a religion or a centrally controlled cult. Useful tests include leader centrality, dissent cost, enemy construction, exit cost, self-sealing explanations and pressure to escalate for belonging. The project therefore uses feature-based comparison rather than blanket diagnosis.

entries.question: What is Continuous Narrative Escalation?
variants: How do Kiwi Farms target threads grow?
How does a harassment narrative escalate online?
entries.short_answer: Continuous Narrative Escalation is a research model describing how online harassment communities can introduce a target, collectively decide how to frame them, and repeatedly add narrative elements that sustain network response.
entries.deep_answer: A 2024 ACM study of 231 Kiwi Farms threads found narrative-building in at least 80% of its sample and described phases of target introduction, network decision and network response. This closely parallels the Potatoverse Strife chain in which knowledge, classification, archive and rediscovery recursively create more material.

entries.question: How does anonymity change online groups?
variants: Does anonymity make people lose control?
What does SIDE theory say about anonymous communities?
entries.short_answer: Anonymity can reduce personal accountability, but social-identity research also shows that it can make group identity and local norms more salient rather than producing pure normlessness.
entries.deep_answer: The SIDE model is especially useful for 4chan-like cultures. When stable personal identity cues are weak, shared language, memes, target categories and board norms can become the stronger basis for behavior. Anonymous communities can therefore become highly norm-governed even without persistent real-name identity.

entries.question: What is online disinhibition?
variants: Why do people say extreme things online?
What is the online disinhibition effect?
entries.short_answer: Online disinhibition is the tendency for some people to disclose or act more freely online because of factors such as anonymity, invisibility, asynchronicity and reduced authority cues.
entries.deep_answer: Suler's classic model identifies dissociative anonymity, invisibility, asynchronicity, solipsistic introjection, dissociative imagination and minimization of authority. The archive treats this as one mechanism among several: disinhibition can amplify behavior, but group norms and incentives determine what direction the amplification takes.

entries.question: What is moral disengagement in online harassment?
variants: How do people justify dogpiling?
How can people harm someone while believing they are good?
entries.short_answer: Moral disengagement is the set of justifications that lets people participate in harmful conduct while preserving a positive self-image.
entries.deep_answer: Common mechanisms include moral justification, euphemistic labeling, diffusion of responsibility, minimizing consequences, dehumanization and victim blame. In a Farm ecology, a target label can make actions feel like deserved entertainment, documentation or public service rather than interpersonal harm.

entries.question: What does classification do in lolcow culture?
variants: Why does calling someone a lolcow matter?
How do labels shape online harassment?
entries.short_answer: Classification does more than describe a person; it supplies an interpretive script for how the audience should read future behavior.
entries.deep_answer: A role-name can behave like a miniature algorithm. Once someone is labeled a lolcow, future statements may be scanned for contradiction, instability or reaction because those are the expected yields. The label can also lower empathy by turning a person into a content category.

entries.question: How do memes create group boundaries on 4chan and similar communities?
variants: Why do insider memes matter?
Are memes a form of status?
entries.short_answer: Memes can operate as cultural capital: knowing when and how to use them signals belonging, while successful innovation can earn status and outsider misuse can mark non-membership.
entries.deep_answer: 4chan scholarship describes memes as part of a subcultural vernacular and as discursive weapons. In the Farm/Sektur model, memes therefore perform three functions at once: entertainment, status competition and boundary enforcement.

entries.question: What is negative parasocial farming?
variants: Why do people obsessively watch someone they hate?
What is hate-watching or anti-fandom?
entries.short_answer: A negative parasocial relationship is sustained attention to a disliked or mocked public figure. It helps explain why hostility can produce long-term attachment rather than disengagement.
entries.deep_answer: Anti-fandom and negative-parasocial research shows that disliked figures can become recurring identity objects. In lolcow culture, this creates a paradox: the audience rejects the target socially while granting them extraordinary attention, detailed memory and ritualized observation. The target becomes structurally central to the group that claims to despise them.

entries.question: Why does a Farm need its Cow?
variants: Why can a harassment community become dependent on its target?
Can a hate community need the person it hates?
entries.short_answer: Because the target can become the ecology's recurring source of events, identity, jokes, status and social cohesion.
entries.deep_answer: If a community's routines and insider culture become organized around one target, complete disappearance of the target can reduce content supply and even weaken group identity. This is one reason negative attention can be relationally dependent: Farmer and Cow roles can become mutually defining even when the relationship is antagonistic.

entries.question: Why can moral outrage become self-reinforcing online?
variants: Why does outrage spread on social media?
Can likes train people to express more outrage?
entries.short_answer: Social feedback and network norms can reinforce outrage expression, making users more likely to repeat forms of moral-emotional language that receive approval.
entries.deep_answer: Research finds both social-learning effects from positive feedback and strong diffusion of moral-emotional language within ideological networks. A Farm or Sektur can therefore shift from entertainment to moral crusade when outrage becomes a prestige-bearing group norm.

entries.question: How do archives keep online conflict alive?
variants: Why do old harassment threads keep returning?
What is archive reactivation?
entries.short_answer: Persistent archives let new users inherit old framing and allow dormant disputes to be rediscovered, quoted and recirculated long after the original event.
entries.deep_answer: Ephemeral imageboards select for fast memetic survival; persistent forums select for cumulative narrative depth. When livestreams, clips, social posts and forum archives cross-link, each medium supplies another with memory or fresh events. The result can be a conflict with a much longer half-life than any single interaction.

entries.question: Why can a target's reaction make an online harassment narrative worse?
variants: Why does responding to trolls sometimes feed them?
Why can correction become more content?
entries.short_answer: In an extraction ecology, a reaction can be interpreted as fresh content and as confirmation that the target is worth continued attention.
entries.deep_answer: Once a target is narratively classified, attempts to rebut, remove or contextualize material can themselves be absorbed into the story. Continuous Narrative Escalation research specifically notes that takedown requests can become narrative elements. This creates a self-sealing risk where responses to the frame are treated as evidence for the frame.

entries.question: What is Moloch historically?
variants: Who was Moloch?
What does Molech mean in the Bible?
entries.short_answer: Moloch/Molech belongs to contested biblical and ancient Near Eastern sacrificial scholarship, especially traditions involving child sacrifice and Tophet contexts; scholars debate whether the term denotes a deity, a sacrificial category or related cultic practice.
entries.deep_answer: The archive now keeps ancient Moloch separate from modern metaphor. Historical scholarship does not justify saying a contemporary website or person literally worships Moloch. The useful connection is comparative: sacrifice and consumed future life become later literary and systems metaphors.

entries.question: How did Allen Ginsberg use Moloch in Howl?
variants: What does Moloch mean in Howl?
Why is Moloch a machine metaphor?
entries.short_answer: Ginsberg transformed Moloch into a symbol for devouring modern machinery and institutions: money, war, alienation, conformity and civilization that consumes human life.
entries.deep_answer: This literary step matters for the Potatoverse because it bridges ancient sacrifice imagery and modern systems critique. Moloch stops being only a cultic-historical problem and becomes an image for structures that demand human possibility as fuel.

entries.question: What does Moloch mean in modern systems thinking?
variants: What is Moloch as coordination failure?
What did Scott Alexander mean by Moloch?
entries.short_answer: In modern rationalist usage, Moloch is a metaphor for destructive competitive or coordination dynamics where individually rewarded choices collectively produce outcomes participants would rather avoid.
entries.deep_answer: This is the strongest non-occult bridge to the Farm. If attention, status or monetization rewards escalation, participants can keep feeding a damaging ecology because unilateral restraint loses local rewards to others. The system can therefore be Moloch-like without any mastermind or literal worship.

entries.question: What is the difference between Farm and Garden in the Potatoverse?
variants: Farm vs Garden
How is a Gardener different from a Farmer?
entries.short_answer: Farm optimizes yield from bounded resources or subjects; Garden optimizes conditions in which living things can develop independent future capacity.
entries.deep_answer: The distinction is functional rather than sentimental. Both may involve boundaries, pruning, selection and repeated labor. The test is whether authority leaves the subject more autonomous, competent and generative or more dependent, captured and harvestable. Farm becomes Moloch-like when present yield destroys future capacity; Garden redesigns incentives around long-horizon growth.

entries.question: What is a self-sealing online community?
variants: What is a self-sealing belief system online?
How can a group make every criticism into proof?
entries.short_answer: A self-sealing community is one whose explanatory system absorbs criticism, contradiction or failed expectations as additional confirmation instead of allowing them to falsify the central narrative.
entries.deep_answer: In drama communities, this can happen when denial becomes guilt, silence becomes suspicious, correction becomes manipulation, departure becomes cowardice and outside criticism becomes enemy coordination. The archive treats falsifiability and preserved disconfirming evidence as key safeguards against Narrative Lock-In.

entries.question: What is Internet Bloodsports?
variants: What are internet bloodsports?
What is livestream bloodsports culture?
entries.short_answer: Internet Bloodsports is a loose online culture of adversarial livestreams, debates, feuds and spectacle in which personalities, audiences, clips and commentary turn conflict into recurring entertainment.
entries.deep_answer: Its importance to the Sektur branch is structural. A stream generates live events; the audience rewards escalation; clippers compress moments; forums interpret and archive them; rival personalities respond; later streams react to the reactions. Conflict becomes a recursive production pipeline rather than a one-time disagreement.
